messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime-service (us-west-2) p95/p99 breach detected by anomaly-detector-v2. p95=420ms (SLO=300ms), p99=1.20s (SLO=0.8s). Spike start ~8201113320. Investigate: https://dashboards.redwood/realtime/alerts/8201113333

oncall-alex: Oncall Alex here, paging SRE. @sre-ryan can you join? Any immediate customer impact?

sre-ryan: Joining. grabbing dashboards and top routes now.

runtime-lee: I see the same — /v1/generate p99 up to 1.4s, streaming tail latency showing stalls and lots of inflight connections queued. KV cache hit rate dropped from ~78% -> ~13% around 8201113300.

pm-kate: Are there 5xx/errors? Support reporting slow responses from a couple EU customers but no elevated 5xx in metrics.

support-jordan: Confirming — no spike in 5xx. Several SLA alerts from large customers complaining about multi-second latency. Ticket volume small but high priority.

infra-maya: Quick infra check: cluster autoscaler in us-west-2 shows no recent scale events. GPU pools at ~85% util; not saturated. Networking egress errors 0.

sre-ryan: Running a narrow query against traces to see tail root cause:
```sql
SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95), percentile(latency_ms, 99), count(*)
FROM traces
WHERE service = 'realtime-service' AND region='us-west-2' AND ts > 8201113200
GROUP BY route
```

sre-ryan: Results: /v1/generate p95=420ms p99=1.4s, /stream/append p95=360ms p99=1.1s. Error patterns show increased KV cache miss latency + more small requests causing many KV lookups.

runtime-lee: We rolled quantized-model-v3 to canary yesterday evening. Canary traffic fraction increased this morning by traffic-shift job. Canary config includes small kv prefix changes — suspect kv miss explosion because of prefix key encoding change.

oncall-alex: If kv miss is root cause, we can fall back traffic to baseline model and/or enable prefix compatibility. Which is faster?

runtime-lee: Fastest: route affected traffic back to model-prod-v2 (baseline) via rollout rollback (takes ~30s to flip routing). Longer: rewarm cache (~several minutes).

sre-ryan: Plan: 1) Flip canary -> prod rollback for realtime service to model-prod-v2 2) Temporarily increase per-route burst capacity for /v1/generate 3) Observe p99 for 5m

pm-kate: Agree. Notify customers if we expect >5m impact.

incident-bot: NOTE: Oncall handoff reminder — mark incident.paging=true if paging external oncall.

oncall-alex: I'm taking lead. @runtime-lee execute rollback, @infra-maya bump burst capacity, @sre-ryan continue telemetry checks.

runtime-lee: Rolling back model routing now: `rwctl rollout set realtime-service --model model-prod-v2 --force`

infra-maya: Increasing per-route burst: `infra-cli scale-route --service realtime-service --route /v1/generate --burst 200` (applied)

sre-ryan: Observability note: enabling additional high-resolution traces for the route (50ms granularity) to catch tail spikes.

incident-bot: MITIGATION_STARTED: rollback triggered at 8201113385 by runtime-lee

sre-ryan: 60s after rollback p95=310ms p99=880ms — p95 is close to SLO, p99 still slightly above.

runtime-lee: Cache hitrate slowly rising from 13% -> 44% after rollback; rewarm in progress.

support-jordan: Customer desk: initial slow alerts still coming in, but new reports are fewer.

oncall-alex: Keep tracking. If p99 doesn't drop below 800ms in next 3m, we'll enable temporary model-fallback routing to dedicated capacity for top customers.

sre-ryan: 3m check: p95=295ms p99=760ms — p99 under SLO now. Trending stable for 2 minutes.

oncall-alex: Good. Marking incident as mitigated. Creating followup ticket to revert canary policy and audit canary traffic-shift job.

pm-kate: Opening customer communication draft for impacted customers. Will share in #support for review.

runtime-lee: Notes for postmortem: cause = canary prefix change -> kv cache miss storm; detection = anomaly-detector-v2 trigger on p99; mitigation = rollback + burst capacity + cache rewarm.

sre-ryan: Action items: (1) add automated check that blocks canary prefix changes without cache-compat flag, (2) add canary rollback auto-trigger when kv miss rate above threshold, (3) add runbook steps for immediate scaling vs rollback.

oncall-alex: Thanks team. Moving to post-incident channel for root cause write-up. If anything else pops, ping me. :thumbsup:
